🐛 Describe the bug
I was looking for a functionality to convert Tensor dtype in-place by passing a string instead of the relevant torch.dtype.
Tensor.type, according to the docs, is supposed to work with dtypes and strs:
def type(self: T, dst_type: Union[dtype, str]) -> T:
        r"""Casts all parameters and buffers to :attr:`dst_type`.

        .. note::
            This method modifies the module in-place.

        Args:
            dst_type (type or string): the desired type

        Returns:
            Module: self
        """

import torch
import numpy as np

x = torch.rand(5,5)
y = np.random.rand(5,5)

🐛 Describe the bug
If we create a new PG using torch.distributed.new_group(torch.tensor([0, 1, 2, 3]), ...), we will end up with ranks in tensor, not int.
For example, if we print out _pg_group_ranks[group] in line 277, it's {tensor(0): 0, tensor(1): 1, tensor(2): 2, tensor(3): 3}.
# From torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py

 265 def _get_group_rank(group: ProcessGroup, rank):
 266     """
 267     Helper that gets a given group's local rank in the group from a given global
 268     rank.
 269     """
 270     if group is GroupMember.WORLD:
 271         raise RuntimeError(
 272             "group.WORLD does not have local rank to global " "rank mapping"
 273         )
 274     if group not in _pg_group_ranks:
 275         raise RuntimeError("The given group does not exist")

🐛 Describe the bug
According to the pytorch's document, if I set center to True the first frame should be centered in the beginning of stft:

  
    
      pytorch/torch/functional.py
    
    
         Line 620
      in
      2367fac
    
  
  
    

        
          
               * If :attr:`center` is ``True`` (default), :attr:`input` will be padded on 
        
    
  


And the following code shows that the stft pads by n_fft//2

  
    
      pytorch/torch/functional.py
    
    
         Line 692
      in
      2367fac
    
  
  
    

        
          
           pad = int(n_fft // 2) 
        
    
  


This works fine in most cases but if the win_length and n_fft are different padding n_fft//2 does not gurantee the first frame be centered. I think win_length//2 is the right choice for the proper operation.

While you took care of this in the tutorial on Transformers and nn.Transformer. I just used nn.TransformerEncoder and realized that this won't initialize parameters in a sensible way on its own. One would create an encoder like this:
encoder_layer = TransformerEncoderLayer(...)
transformer_encoder = TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, nlayers) 

This will yield a Transformer that has the same initialization in all layers, which I think rarely is what you want in neural networks, so it is unexpected. You always need to initialize from the outside again. This is not the usual case in PyTorch and not documented, see https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.TransformerEncoder.html#torch.nn.TransformerEncoder
I am not sure which way to better resolve this, through a changed nn.TransformerEncoder API, just documentation or whether you are working on a rewrite anyways already. Thus, I raised this as an issue first.
Versions
This is a problem in the current version (1.10). This bug does not need to be reproduced, but can be seen relatively easy from the source code of nn.TransformerEncoder.

🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
The native index_select on sparse COO tensors has been reported to be slow in the past (see #61788 and #54561). While improvements have been made with #63008, it remains slower than expected even with pytorch 1.10.0 and 1.10.1 which, as per the 1.10.0 release notes, I understand include the #63008 patch.
Alternatives
The index_select implementation from rusty1s/torch_sparse can be used in lieu of the native index_select and it is sometimes up to 1000x faster.
Additional context
Below is the simple test case I used as a quick and dirty "benchmark" (also on colab):

Currently, the following functions in torch.nn.init are routed through __torch_function__ for custom tensors:

uniform_
normal_
kaiming_uniform_

Arguably, these should not be directly overrideable using __torch_function__, and calls to the Python API for the underlying ATen ops should show up instead.
For the example of kaiming_uniform_, this would allow custom tensors to reuse the bounds calculation and simply override tensor.uniform_ instead. Right now, failing to provide a kaiming_uniform_ impl in __torch_function__ for a given custom tensor will error out when the function is called, even if uniform_ is provided, due to a lack of __torch_function__ re-dispatch.
Is there any use case that requires these init functions to be handled directly for a custom tensor?

🐛 Describe the bug
When using a simple, modified version of MNIST dataset returning pairs of input, I encountered a weird bug preventing training when using the cross_entropy loss function. I needed a double-digit version on MNIST to train of different possibility of targets (sum, 100 class etc...). However, on a simple case scenario optimization failed. It had to do with my indexing of an 2 column target AFTER sending it to the GPU. That resulted in a non contiguous tensor (stride 2). Any operation on the target made training possible again, but the in appearance the simplest of all tasks (predicting 1st digit only) seemed not to train. Actually, the loss actually goes back up when training with non-contiguous version of the target, even on a properly trained model.
Solution : make target contiguous again using .contiguous(), or for that matter any operation such as target = target + 1 - 1
This is my first time reporting a bug so hopes it helps and is not to messy !! All the best
Python :
`
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader
import torch
from torchvision import transforms, datasets
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from tqdm.notebook import tqdm
import os

if use_cuda:
    cuda_kwargs = {'num_workers': 0,
                'pin_memory': True
                }
    train_kwargs.update(cuda_kwargs)

root = os.path.expanduser("~/Code/Data/MNIST")
transformations= transforms.Compose(
    [transforms.ToTensor(), 
    transforms.Normalize((0.1307,), (0.3081,))
    ])

class DoubleMNIST(Dataset) :
    """
    Double Digits MNIST dataset    
    """
    
    def __init__(self, root, train=True, transforms=None):
        super().__init__()

        self.transform=transforms
        dataset = datasets.MNIST(root, train=train, download=False,
                transform=self.transform)
        self.mnist_dataset = dataset
        self.secondary_index = torch.randperm(len(self.mnist_dataset))

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        index_1= index
        index_2 = self.secondary_index[index]

        digit_1, target_1 = self.mnist_dataset[index_1]
        digit_2, target_2 = self.mnist_dataset[index_2]

        digits = torch.cat([digit_1, digit_2], axis = 0)
        targets = [target_1, target_2]

        return digits, torch.tensor(targets)

    def __len__(self) : 
        return len(self.mnist_dataset)

double_dataset = DoubleMNIST(root, True, transformations)
loader = DataLoader(double_dataset, **train_kwargs)

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(784, 100), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(100, 10)).to(device)
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

pbar = tqdm(range(1))

model.train()

        data, target = batch[0].to(device), batch[1].to(device)
        data, target = data[:, 0].flatten(start_dim=-2), target[:, 0]

        optimizer.zero_grad()
        output = model(data)

        assert target.shape == output.shape[:-1], print(target.shape, output.shape)

        loss = F.cross_entropy(output, target, reduction='mean')
            
        pred = output.argmax(dim=-1)  # get the index of the max log-probability
        correct = pred.eq(target.view_as(pred)).sum().item()
        acc = correct/target.numel()
        
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()

        desc = str('Train Epoch: {} [{}/{} ({:.0f}%)] Loss: {:.3f}, Acc:{}'.format(
                epoch, batch_idx * loader.batch_size, len(loader.dataset),

There's an edge case that existing Composite Compliance testing does not test. Right now, Composite Compliance testing works by wrapping ALL tensors in a CompositeCompliantTensor and sending it through a function.
With Tensor subclasses, some, but not necessarily all, tensor arguments to a function will be Tensor Subclasses. This is important to test as well because it will catch the following non-composite-compliant behavior:
def my_composite_operator(x, y):
  x.inplace_(y)
  return x

The above is not composite compliant because if y is Tensor Subclass but x isn't, then it isn't possible to write y in-place to x.
cc @mruberry @albanD @zou3519

As mentioned here: #69827 (comment)
forward AD in PyTorch is supposed to work with inputs with requires_grad=False. However, we don't test for it, because we use gradcheck to test forward-AD and gradcheck currently does not support Tensors that do not require gradients.
We should either:

🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
We currently only have an API called _init_from_local_shards which actually performs an allgather: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/distributed/_sharded_tensor/api.py#L351. We need a variation of this that doesn't do the validation for perf reasons or have a separate simpler API.
One proposal here is to have a new API like the following:
def from_local_tensor(tensor: torch.Tensor, *size: Sequence[int], spec: ShardingSpec) -> ShardedTensor

Each local rank can build the sharding metadata locally to avoid more expensive allgather. After implementing this, we then need to update the place where _init_from_local_shards is not necessary.

🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
The behavior of mean reduction in nn.CrossEntropy and nn.NLLLoss is counter intuitive when there are class weights as discussed in #9882. The current behavior performs a weighted average instead of an unweighted average, which is probably what people expect.
This counter intuitive behavior also causes an issue when doing  gradient accumulation. In particular, when you adjust the loss function to account for gradient accumulation (i.e. to make the divisor batch_size x n_grad_accum_steps instead of just batch_size) you no longer have the exact gradients (i.e. the gradients you would have had if your batch size was batch_size x n_grad_accum_steps).
# Example gradient accumulation code
# loader, model, optimizer, weights set above 

# unweighted case -- no issue for gradient accumulation
loss_func = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction='mean')

# weighted case with an issue
# loss_func = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weights=weights, reduction='mean')

# this loop assumes everything is nicely divisible -- it can be modified to handle when
# num batches is not divisible by grad_accum and num_samples is not divisible by batch_size
for batch_idx, (x, y_true) in enumerate(loader):
    y_pred = model(x)
    loss = loss_func(y_true, y_pred) 
    
    # adjust for gradient accumulation
    # this gives you exact gradients in the unweighted case, but not in the weighted case!
    loss = loss / n_grad_accum_batches
    
    loss.backward()
    if (batch_idx + 1) % n_grad_accum_batches == 0:
        optimizer.step()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
You can of course address this issue if you use reduction=sum and manually averaging the loss, but this is clunky and probably frequently overlooked.
Possible solution
A straightforward solution and the most intuitive -- at least to me -- would be

make reduction='mean' perform an unweighted average
introduce reduction='weighted_mean' for weighted averages (current behavior of mean)
default to to the unweighted mean  case, which is probably what users expect to happen
